summary: Frontend-only smoke test of Step-1 normal-mapped lighting rebuild (player body + hydropistol projectiles as GLSL-filtered sprites). FOUND A CRITICAL, 100%-REPRODUCIBLE CRASH: the moment PixiRenderer initializes (which happens as soon as gameplay/welcome-fight starts), the browser throws an uncaught TypeError inside PixiJS's shader-compilation pipeline while building the new lit filter, and a React/CRA dev error overlay ('Uncaught runtime errors:') covers the entire screen. Reproduced this identically across 3 separate fresh sessions (different character names) -- every single attempt to reach gameplay crashed at the exact same stack frame. Because of this, NONE of the requested visual verification items (lit player body highlight, muzzle-flash brightening, lit hydropistol bullets, old-lighting-removed regression) could be completed -- the game is effectively unplayable/unviewable past this point (canvas renders behind the overlay but is fully obscured and the app is in a broken error state).

ui_bugs.issue: Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'substring') thrown from PixiJS internals (Object.ensurePrecision -> new _GlProgram -> _GlProgram.from -> _Filter.from) when _makeLitFilter() calls Filter.from({ gl: { fragment: this._litFragment }, resources: {...} }). This happens on EVERY session as soon as the gameplay canvas/PixiRenderer initializes (observed right after 'ENTER THE LAKE' -> welcome-fight starts). The dev error overlay covers the whole screen; the underlying game HUD (timer, wave, kills) is visible ticking behind it, confirming the game loop keeps running in a broken state while the shader/filter never successfully compiled -- meaning this.playerBodyFilter and the 16-sprite hydropistol filter pool are effectively non-functional going forward. Likely root cause: Filter.from's internal _GlProgram builder expects a fully-formed shader source (version pragma / precision qualifier) that PixiJS auto-derives from vertex+fragment pairing, and something in how _litFragment is passed (fragment-only, no explicit vertex, or resource/uniform shape under gl.fragment) causes an internal array entry to be undefined before .substring() is called on it. This is a shader-registration-format issue specific to this PixiJS v8 build, not a GLSL syntax typo per se.

integration_issues.issue: Flow works perfectly up through intro dialogue (AIDA dialogue screen renders correctly, zero errors). The crash happens exactly when PixiRenderer (the game canvas) initializes, which is the very first frame gameplay would be visible. So the regression smoke test scope (movement/aiming/shooting/leveling/pausing) also could not be exercised at all this pass -- not because those systems are broken, but because the app is stuck behind this fatal error overlay before any gameplay interaction is possible.

action_items: BLOCKING: Fix PixiRenderer._makeLitFilter's Filter.from({gl:{fragment}, resources:{...}}) call -- it throws inside PixiJS's internal shader-precision/GlProgram builder (Object.ensurePrecision reading undefined.substring()) on 100% of sessions the moment the game canvas initializes, making the ENTIRE GAME unplayable past intro dialogue (game is stuck behind a full-screen 'Uncaught runtime errors' overlay). Full stack: Object.ensurePrecision -> new _GlProgram -> _GlProgram.from -> _Filter.from -> PixiRenderer._makeLitFilter -> _buildNormalLitSystem -> _buildLayers.

Suspect the Filter.from() call needs an explicit vertex shader (or the exact gl:{vertex, fragment} pairing PixiJS v8's filter pipeline expects) rather than fragment-only, or the resources block shape (extraTextures / uLight uniform group naming) doesn't match what this PixiJS version's GlProgram builder expects when deriving precision qualifiers -- recommend checking PixiJS v8's Filter.from() docs/examples for the exact required shape and comparing against _makeLitFilter's current call, since a fragment-only custom filter should be a well-supported pattern in v8.

Once fixed, this entire visual test suite (lit player body highlight across aim angles, muzzle-flash brightening, lit hydropistol bullets, confirm old lighting fully removed) needs to be re-run from scratch -- none of it was reachable this pass due to the blocking crash.
critical_code_review_comments: pixiRenderer.js _buildNormalLitSystem: the analytical normal-map baking (canvas ImageData sphere math) and the flat diffuse circle texture generation look correct on code review and are NOT implicated in the crash (the crash is specifically in _makeLitFilter's Filter.from call, downstream of successful texture creation).

pixiRenderer.js _litFragment GLSL: uses `in vec2 vTextureCoord; out vec4 finalColor;` (GLSL ES 3.00 / WebGL2 style) without an explicit `#version 300 es` line at the top of the string -- if PixiJS v8's Filter.from() expects the raw fragment string to already include the version pragma when using `in`/`out` syntax (rather than auto-injecting it), that mismatch could plausibly be the root cause of the internal precision-parsing crash; worth checking against a working v8 custom-filter example.

pixiRenderer.js _drawPlayer / _drawLitHydroProjectiles: downstream calls to this._updateLitUniforms(this.playerBodyFilter, ...) and per-pool-item filter access will themselves throw/no-op if this.playerBodyFilter et al ended up undefined or partially-constructed after the Filter.from exception -- worth wrapping _buildNormalLitSystem in a try/catch with a safe fallback (e.g. skip lit-sprite rendering and fall back to the old poly-fill) so a shader compile failure doesn't take down the entire render loop and app for a scoped smoke-test feature.

General: for a 'step 1 smoke test' this narrow, a defensive try/catch around the new Filter.from() construction (falling back gracefully to a flat-tinted sprite if the filter fails to build) would have prevented this single new code path from crashing the entire game, which is a good practice for isolated experimental render features going forward.

rca of the issue: Root cause: PixiJS v8's internal shader-program builder (_GlProgram / Object.ensurePrecision) throws when parsing the custom fragment shader registered via Filter.from({gl:{fragment: this._litFragment}, resources:{...}}) inside PixiRenderer._makeLitFilter(). The exact internal field that is undefined before .substring() is called is not visible from the stack trace alone (it's inside PixiJS's minified bundle), but the most likely candidates are: (a) the fragment-only GLSL ES 3.00 source string (using `in`/`out` syntax) is missing an explicit `#version 300 es` pragma that this PixiJS build expects the caller to supply rather than auto-inject, or (b) the resources/uniform-group shape passed to Filter.from (extraTextures + a named uLight uniform group with typed entries) doesn't exactly match what this PixiJS version's Filter.from() convenience API expects, causing it to construct a malformed/incomplete GlProgram config downstream. Reproduction: fresh browser session -> create any character -> click ENTER THE LAKE -> click through intro dialogue until gameplay starts -> crash fires immediately and consistently, 3/3 sessions. Mitigation for future similar work: wrap experimental Filter.from()/shader construction in try/catch with a safe non-shader fallback so a single new render feature's compile failure can't take down the entire app during a scoped smoke-test rollout.
